fix.mechanism: Wednesday pads its audio slice with silence to exactly the generated duration: T1 holds 10.7612s of speech inside a 12.0s slice for a 12s generation, with lead_zero_pad_s 0.05 and lead_silence_total_s 0.4. With the audio running the full clip length the model has nothing to stretch into.
fix.mine_was: 6.542s of speech supplied against an 8s generation, so the model filled the gap by slowing down.
fix.correction: Pad every slice to its exact generation length, lead pad plus speech plus trailing silence.
fix.side_benefit: The trailing silence is the trim headroom, so takes no longer need the extra second of generation. Generating at ceil(speech) instead of ceil(speech)+1 cuts the batch from 651 to 588.

batch_plan_v2.change: generate at ceil(speech seconds), with the audio slice padded to the same length

measurement_correction.what_i_reported: Take 1 stretched its speech by +1.46s, about 22 percent, worse than the drift that failed this episode's long form.
measurement_correction.what_is_true: Measured directly from the audio envelope in 20ms windows, take 1's speech runs 0.50 to 7.38, a 6.88s span against the reference slice's 6.44s. The real stretch is +0.44s, about 7 percent.
measurement_correction.why_i_was_wrong: I took the figure from Whisper word timings. On take 1 it put the last word at 8.00s, and on take 2 it put the last word at 8.32s inside a 7.07s clip, which is impossible. Whisper's word-end timings overrun file boundaries and are not a timing measurement. This is the second time in this session that the same artifact has misled me: it also produced the false end-overrun reading on the narration guides.
measurement_correction.method_lesson: For speech timing, measure the audio envelope. ASR establishes words, not when they happen.
measurement_correction.cost_of_the_error: 49 credits on a second take designed to fix an overstated fault.

second_take.slice: 0.4s lead silence, 6.542s speech, 0.058s trail, padded to exactly 7.000s
second_take.finding: Padding did not remove the timing error, it reversed its sign. Take 2 starts 0.44s late and speaks 0.92s fast, about 14 percent compressed, against take 1's 0.44s slow. The model does not follow the audio reference's timing closely in either configuration.

revised_reading.take_1_may_be_usable: At +0.44s over a 6.44s span, take 1 sits inside the sub-0.7s drift band that EP007's accepted takes held. I called it unusable on a measurement that was wrong.
revised_reading.untested_step: The accepted Wednesday route runs fal-ai/sync-lipsync/react-1 over every take. That pass exists to absorb exactly this residual drift, and I have not run it. Judging either take before it is judging an unfinished stage.
revised_reading.honest_position: Neither take is proven good or bad yet, and the padding hypothesis is disproved.
